purpose: Candidate retrieval, scoped feature lookup, and concept-graph membership. LLM review decides identity and applicability.

object.definition: The action set is a public metric space $(\mathcal X,D)$ of diameter at most $1$, possibly with infinitely many arms; the required covering and activation interfaces are available. Each arm has $m$ fixed mean rewards $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m$, ordered by priority, and every mean function is $1$-Lipschitz. Each objective has oscillation at most $1$; irrelevant common additive shifts are unrestricted. A lexicographically optimal arm $x^\star$ exists. Ties are allowed at each priority; subsequent objectives are compared among arms optimal for all higher-priority objectives. The tradeoff coefficient is finite: $$\lambda_\star=\inf\!\left\{\lambda\ge0:\ \mu_i(x)-\mu_i(x^\star)\le\lambda\max_{j<i}\bigl(\mu_j(x^\star)-\mu_j(x)\bigr),\ \forall x\in\mathcal X,\ 2\le i\le m\right\}<\infty.$$ $$N_c(r)=\min\!\left\{n:\ \mathcal X\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{n}B_D(x_j,r),\ x_j\in\mathcal X\right\}.$$ Here $N_c(r)$ is the covering number at radius $r$. The objective-specific zooming quantities $N_z^{(i)}(r)$ use the source definitions on the corresponding near-optimal regions and cannot be replaced by the ambient dimension $d$.

operation.query_signature: Choose an arm $x_t$, then observe all $m$ reward coordinates of that arm. Conditional on past observations and the current arm, each coordinate is $1$-sub-Gaussian around its fixed mean; coordinates need not be independent. $$\mathbb E\!\left[e^{s(Y_{t,i}-\mu_i(x_t))}\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},x_t\right]\le e^{s^2/2}\qquad(s\in\mathbb R,\ 1\le i\le m).$$ Causal policies may use the public covering and activation interfaces. The metric space, $m,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$, and $\lambda\ge\lambda_\star$ are public. The mean functions and lexicographically optimal arm $x^\star$ are hidden. Observed feedback may be stored and reused computationally; unrevealed past information and additional queries to exhausted samples are unavailable. Any within-round full-function or common-sample two-point access must be explicitly specified.

definition.arms: known metric (X,D) of diameter <=1, each mu_i is 1-Lipschitz; required covering/activation oracles are available
definition.mean_range: objective mean ranges have diameter <=1; additive offsets are immaterial
definition.objectives: m ordered objectives with a lexicographically optimal arm x_star (ties allowed)
definition.tradeoff: lambda_star=inf{lambda>=0: mu_i(x)-mu_i(x_star)<=lambda max_{j<i}[mu_j(x_star)-mu_j(x)] for all i>=2,x}; restrict to finite lambda_star

protocols.adversary_information: Follow the model and oracle timing. Current private random realizations are not visible to the environment.
protocols.loss_bearing_points: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.
protocols.past_requery: History may be stored. New information from old samples or past rounds is unavailable unless the native interface explicitly permits it.
steps: Select arm $x_t$ first, then observe all $m$ coordinates of its reward vector.
Given the past and the current arm, each reward coordinate is conditionally $1$-sub-Gaussian around its fixed mean. Independence between objective coordinates is not required.
Causal strategies may use the public metric-covering or activation interface. The metric space, $m,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$, and $\lambda\ge\lambda_\star$ are public.
Mean functions and the lexicographically optimal arm $x^\star$ are hidden.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.
